title: 讲座的层次与要点
goal: 识别讲座的论述层次；确定问题对应的信息类别。

points.label: 确定问题对应的信息类别

sources.title: 大学英语六级（CET-6）：课表
sources.used: 讲座的教学内容、知识点与练习规格

body.p: 讲座一般分四层。主题是整段讨论的核心问题。概念解释说明术语或过程。论据提供观察、数据或实例。结论归纳前面的内容。一句话属于哪一层，看它在上下文中的作用。

body.box: Today we'll consider how labels affect the use of a seed collection. A label is a record of a sample's identity. In one collection, several samples lacked dates. Clear records make samples easier to compare.

body.p: 首句提出主题，第二句解释 label，第三句给出实例，末句说明记录的作用。缺少日期是论据，不是整段的主题。

steps.d: 主题看两处：开头提出的问题，后面反复解释的对象。For example 引出的实例只说明主题的一个方面。
概念解释说明术语或过程。论据提供支持判断的材料。A sample is a selected part 是定义，The team examined twenty samples 是论据。
先看选项是定义、数字还是建议，再确定要听哪一类信息。A sample is a selected part 是定义，Record the date 是建议。
结论要和前文的论述一致。原文用记录不全说明需要改进，结论就是改进记录。记录不全本身是论据。

cards.title: 讲座的论述层次
rows: How can a seed collection remain useful?
A sample is a selected part of a collection.
Several samples had no collection date.
cards.note: 含数字的句子也可能是定义的一部分。判断层次时看这句话的作用。

cards.title: 信息类别
rows: A sample is a selected part.
Record the date for each sample.
说明讨论开始前的情况
The collection began as a small donation.
cards.note: 数字要连同它的对象一起记。同一个数字可能属于不同的对象。

body.box: A community archive wants its photographs to remain useful. Today I'll discuss the records that accompany them. A caption identifies the people, place or event shown in an image. In one group of pictures, dates were missing, so visitors could not arrange the images in sequence. The archive now checks each caption against its existing records. The experience suggests that a photograph and its documentation should be preserved together.

What is the function of the reference to missing dates?
1. It provides an example of incomplete documentation.
2. It defines a caption as a sequence of photographs.
3. It states the archive's final recommendation.
4. It describes the original reason for creating the archive.

body.p: dates were missing 是资料不完整的实例，属于论据，即第一项。第三项把它当成了结论。讲座的结论在末句：a photograph and its documentation should be preserved together。

cards.title: 干扰项
rows: Missing dates are the entire subject of the talk.
实例只是论据，范围比主题小。
A caption identifies people, so it is the proposed action.
定义说明术语的意思，建议说明要做的事。
The archive's initial collection is its final judgment.
结论在末尾，归纳前文的内容。
Twenty labels were missing when twenty samples were checked.
把数字对应到原文中它所属的对象。

lines.text: A museum is considering how visitors find their way through its rooms. A route map represents the connections between those rooms. One trial found that visitors overlooked a corridor when its entrance was unmarked. The staff therefore proposed a clearer sign at that entrance.

items.stem: What role does the overlooked corridor play?
options: It supplies an example of a navigation difficulty.
It defines the route map as a sign at an entrance.
It states the staff's proposed improvement to the entrance.
It describes the connections that the route map represents.
items.why: visitors overlooked a corridor 是寻路困难的实例，即第一项。

lines.text: A workshop measures drying time for clay objects. Drying time means the interval between shaping an object and firing it. Six bowls were checked each morning. The instructor recommends recording the room conditions as well as the time.

items.stem: Which information defines the term drying time?
options: The number of bowls checked each morning
The interval between shaping and firing
The conditions recorded in the room
The instructor's suggested record keeping
items.why: Drying time means the interval between shaping an object and firing it 给出定义，即第二项。

lines.text: A town is considering the upkeep of its footpaths. Last year a fallen branch blocked one path for a week. That case illustrates why a reporting system matters. The council suggests giving residents a single contact for reporting obstacles.

options: Clear fallen branches from the footpaths within a week.
Give each footpath its own contact for residents' reports.
Ask residents to record how long obstacles block a path.
Provide residents with one contact for reporting obstacles.
items.why: 依据是 suggests giving residents a single contact for reporting obstacles，即第四项。第二项把 single contact 改成了每条小路各一个。

lines.text: A school is examining how to store musical instruments. A damaged case is one example of a storage problem. Other cases are sound but lack labels. The speaker concludes that both condition and identification need regular attention.

items.stem: Which statement expresses the overall conclusion?
options: A damaged case is the only problem that needs attention.
Labels eliminate the need to inspect the condition of cases.
Storage requires checks of condition and identification.
Storage requires regular checks of the cases' condition.
items.why: 依据是 both condition and identification need regular attention，即第三项。第四项只说了状况，漏掉了标签。

lines.text: A library is reviewing the use of its meeting rooms. A booking record is the information kept about a reservation, including the room and time. Last month staff examined thirty records; five lacked an end time. This gap made it difficult to see when a room would be free. The library plans to require an end time on each booking. The general lesson is that a useful reservation system needs information about both the beginning and the end of an event.

items.stem: What role does the reference to five records play?
options: It defines a reservation as a room and a time.
It gives evidence of incomplete booking information.
It states the proposed requirement for all bookings.
It states the general lesson about reservation systems.
items.why: five lacked an end time 是记录不完整的证据，即第二项。

items.stem: Which figure describes the records examined?
options: Five records without a room
Five records with an end time
Thirty records missing a time
Thirty records in the review
items.why: staff examined thirty records 说明被检查的记录共 thirty，即第四项。

options: Reservations need both starting and finishing information.
Missing end times prove that every meeting room is occupied.
A room number alone establishes the full reservation period.
A review of thirty records replaces the existing booking system.
items.why: both the beginning and the end of an event 归纳记录需要的时间信息，即第一项。

lines.text: Today I want to discuss how a collection of oral histories can remain useful to people who were not present at the interviews. Recording a voice is essential, but a sound file by itself doesn't explain every circumstance in which the conversation took place. An archive also needs a consistent way to describe the recording. I'll explain what such a description contains, consider a small example, and then return to the purpose of the record. An interview record is a written account of basic information about a recording. It can identify the date, the interviewer, the contributor, and the topics discussed. It is not a substitute for listening to the interview. Instead, it helps someone decide which recording may be relevant and understand the context before listening. Imagine an archive that receives a box of recorded interviews about local food preparation. Some files have descriptive notes, but others have only numbers. A volunteer listens to twenty recordings and finds that four have no date in their accompanying notes. Those four recordings can still be heard, but their place in a sequence of interviews is uncertain. Adding a date when reliable evidence is available may make comparison easier. The archive also needs to distinguish a date written on a container from a date confirmed by a contributor. The first is a clue; the second has been checked against another source. If the two disagree, the record should retain the uncertainty rather than present one date as settled without explanation. A short note about the evidence can help a later listener interpret the difference. The same care applies to names and topics. A name may be spelled in more than one way, and a brief topic list cannot contain every detail of a long conversation. Staff can record alternative spellings and describe the main subjects without claiming that the list is complete. The lesson from the example is that an archive preserves more than sound. It also preserves information that makes a recording findable and interpretable. A useful record identifies what is known, indicates where it came from, and leaves unresolved questions visible.

options: It reports a volunteer's findings and then lists every missing date.
It compares records with sound files and prefers the sound files alone.
It defines a record, illustrates a difficulty, and draws a conclusion.
It describes a box of recordings and recommends discarding its notes.
items.why: An interview record is 引出定义，缺少日期是实例，结尾归纳记录的作用，即第三项。

items.stem: Which statement gives the definition of an interview record?
options: It is a collection of recorded voices without any accompanying notes.
It is a written description of basic information about a recording.
It is a complete written transcript of every conversation in an archive.
It is a date confirmed by a contributor during an interview.
items.why: An interview record is a written account of basic information about a recording 给出定义，即第二项。

items.stem: What does the example of the four recordings contribute?
options: It provides evidence of missing dates in descriptive notes.
It proves every container date was confirmed by a contributor.
It states the archive's complete policy for alternative spellings.
It defines a topic list as a sequence of interview dates.
items.why: four have no date in their accompanying notes 是日期缺失的实例，即第一项。

lines.text: The question for this talk is how a community garden can decide when its shared watering equipment needs attention. A hose may look intact and still have a small leak, while a dry tap may be the result of a temporary interruption in supply. The aim is to keep those possibilities separate and make a useful decision about maintenance. First, consider the meaning of an inspection. Here an inspection is a planned check of equipment against a short list of observable conditions. It might include looking for cracks, checking the fittings, and noting whether water flows when the tap is open. An inspection describes what was observed at a particular time; it does not automatically establish the cause of a problem. During one fictional trial, a garden team checked twelve hoses. Three had loose fittings, and one of those three also had a visible crack. The team recorded both observations for that hose rather than counting it as a different hose for each fault. In addition, the team noted that a tap was dry that morning. A later check showed that supply to the garden had been temporarily interrupted, so the dry tap alone did not establish a fault in the hose. These observations support a practical distinction. The number of faults is not necessarily the number of pieces of equipment affected. Also, a single observation may have more than one possible explanation. The team can tighten a loose fitting, but it should inspect a cracked hose separately before deciding whether to repair or replace it. What should be kept in the record? The team recommends writing down the item, the condition observed, and the date of the check. If the cause remains uncertain, that uncertainty should be recorded too. A later inspection can then be compared with the earlier one without treating an assumption as a measured result. The wider conclusion is that maintenance decisions depend on clear observations linked to the correct item. A count without that connection can make the scale of a problem difficult to judge. A recommendation is an action proposed in response to evidence, while the observations themselves describe what the team actually found.

items.stem: Which figure represents the hoses examined in the trial?
options: Three hoses with no loose fitting
One hose with no visible crack
Twelve hoses with loose fittings
Twelve hoses checked by the team
items.why: a garden team checked twelve hoses 说明检查的对象和数量，即第四项。

items.stem: Which statement gives the team's recommendation for records?
options: Treat each fault as a separate hose in the count.
Record the item, observed condition, and inspection date.
Assume a dry tap proves that a hose is damaged.
Replace every hose with a loose fitting immediately.
items.why: writing down the item, the condition observed, and the date 是记录建议，即第二项。

items.stem: What function does the dry tap example serve?
options: It defines an inspection as a list of items to replace.
It states that the garden's supply is permanently interrupted.
It illustrates that one observation can have different explanations.
It concludes that all hoses with loose fittings are cracked.
items.why: dry tap 与 temporary interruption 说明一次观察可能有不同解释，即第三项。
